state_summary: Round 4, seed 157, free_llm32_dual_expert_v1: the packet reports 461 measured records, 2,869 legal candidates, no pending experiments and no validation/test records. Latest feedback emphasizes m173's endpoint-specific tail, m125's loading-solvent interaction and excessive transfer between related structures. Several earlier response-curve questions are substantially resolved. Expected improvements in overall Row accuracy remain inferences; historical acquisition errors do not establish retrained performance.
important_observations: [Observed and historical predictions; new H9] m173 at fixed sample volume 100 ul and DCM loading-solvent volume 2,000 ul changes from V1/V2 5.117/50.300 ml at 0/1 to 6.508/108.892 ml at 1/1 (6802f0b28c5a0c7b4c2a, f90a5a5a54509c085ebd). The proposed V2 contraction is contradicted. Historical errors at 1/1 were -1.836/-94.983 ml, showing a predominantly V2 failure. Persistence, a local maximum and reproducibility remain unresolved.

[Observed; H5 revised] m125's loading-solvent effect extends to 1/1. At sample volume 50 ul, changing DCM loading-solvent volume from 300 to 500 ul changes endpoints from 9.250/18.350 to 12.492/36.142 ml (00043aebb2540e369a7b, f4fb5c03b8e8996e75f6); at 100 ul, it changes 7.500/20.467 to 13.442/38.400 ml (4c32851430464f0ed684, dbb94bf062fc0e640258). With 500 ul loading solvent, the 50/100/150 ul sample series is comparatively smooth: V1 12.492/13.442/14.067 and V2 36.142/38.400/39.383 ml, including 9bd998a328b109ef639e. This weakens any explanation requiring the anomalous 2/1 V1 valley at every ratio. The valley at 69b09343d0b9995c3ae4 still needs reproducibility evidence.

[Observed and historical predictions; H3 strengthened through rejected generalizations] A common signed alcohol or beta-ketoester correction is unsupported. At 5/1 and sample volume 100 ul, m205 measures 51.433/98.375 ml (48853fd78c77153b963a), whereas m206 measures 26.058/57.808 ml (614873124b33029a924c). Their loading-solvent volumes also differ, preventing structure-only attribution. m107 has a real 5/1 tail (c6924324ddd95f249df6), but its subsequently measured 2/1 points were overpredicted (143bf510fe2028583763, 769f1d04efb22c05cfdf). m13 at 2/1 measures only 9.042/18.167 ml, with historical errors +19.423/+50.687 ml (2dbfdf9c2d5defd09f7a). Conversely, tertiary amine m19 at 2/1 measures 23.692/34.825 ml, with errors -17.112/-24.429 ml (6d21e9ec887b3408c612). Residual sign and tail magnitude depend on structure and condition.

[Observed; H2 supported locally] At m107 2/1, increasing sample volume from 50 to 150 ul changes endpoints from 21.733/45.667 to 14.150/42.350 ml (143bf510fe2028583763, 769f1d04efb22c05cfdf). At m216 10/1, V1 decreases 53.417 to 45.800 to 42.925 ml across 50/100/150 ul, while V2 remains approximately 93 ml (e47aebe2660b9e1528de, 9cd02352c2ed7a3e2321, 222a68fc192f66c1c080). Endpoint-specific interactions are supported; repeatability and causal mechanisms remain unproven.

[Observed; H7 more constrained] m92 with EA 200 ul loading solvent now has intermediate-ratio anchors at both sample volumes. At 50 ul, V2 is 26.350/34.550/58.542 ml at 10/1, 20/1 and 50/1 (0389a6366b3a51fad8b5, 66da447ca0fe7160cc1c, 7caf1db075b91197ba34); at 100 ul, it is 28.150/29.625/61.950 ml (4b8ba288d549f6cfc94b, 8b58e9d7a710f55e49d3, 7b42519983cf93dd7efd). Loading directions differ between ratios. Latest intermediate-point historical V2 errors were about -2.1 to -2.2 ml, reducing the case for routine grid expansion.

[Observed; H8 strengthened] New m146 2/1 anchors (cf36dbeee8bb51632d84, 2745c6978a8911fc3dda), m31 intermediate/baseline points (2a4de703709973e74dd2, d6ef05c62d2172fae39a) and m212 baselines (ab4326dd3bd3b0e07f81, 18a189c89f59ac1d5a9f) constrain distinct response shapes. Fixed-load m193 V2 rises from 44.292 at 10/1 to 78.533 ml at 20/1 (a01a137fa48c1391b9e7, a5f9179bfb146ad70953). These measurements do not establish smoothness throughout unmeasured intervals or a shared tail law.

[Observed; H1/H6 retained, H4 rejected] m167 remains a densely measured V2-dominant response curve; m147 remains a shallow-response anchor. Routine expansion of these molecules and m105 has diminishing value. The endpoint-order premise remains rejected by ordered measured endpoints and recorded predictions for 81507d463506a9e65e73 and 3a095d378b537020c569.
important_model_behaviors: [Current predictions only] m173 now predicts a V2 maximum near 1/1 in the 1,500 ul loading-solvent context: approximately 106.190 ml at 1/1, 90.024 at 2/1 and 74.836 at 5/1. Only the measured 0/1-to-1/1 increase in the 2,000 ul context is established. The predicted maximum is a useful competing response shape.

[Current predictions only] Loading sensitivity remains weak across many grids. m173 5/1 predicts 13.625/74.836 ml with DCM 1,500 ul versus 13.619/74.877 ml with 2,000 ul; density also changes slightly. m19 2/1 predictions at sample volumes 100 and 150 ul are likewise almost identical. Agreement between predictions does not establish negligible loading effects.

[Current predictions only] m13 2/1 predictions have contracted to approximately 8.24/18.12 ml, while 5/1 still predicts 31.28/73.27 ml and 10/1 approximately 48.18/102.26 ml. The remaining tail is unverified. A same-load 5/1 measurement can distinguish delayed tail onset from continuing overtransfer.

[Current output diagnostic] Quantiles remain unsuitable for direct uncertainty ranking: V1 q10 repeatedly equals zero and some q50 values exceed q90. Candidate 5d11af6ff834c7706e64 has V2 q10/q50/q90 8.570/8.836/8.374 ml and negative reported width. The earlier crossing at 89d752b5a7f7c8d0b91e is currently resolved; reassess anomalies each round.

[Historical predictions] m205's latest 5/1, 50 ul V2 prediction missed by only +0.154 ml after an earlier severe underprediction at 100 ul. This is consistent with local adaptation, but successive models and different conditions prevent interpreting it as proof of overall Row improvement.
possible_learning_bottlenecks: [Inference] Tail labels may distort related molecules or adjacent ratios. m205/m206 and m107/m13 provide measured counterexamples. Contrasts separating molecule offsets from ratio slopes should be more efficient than repeatedly sampling extreme predictions.

[Inference] Weak predicted loading sensitivity may reflect feature scaling, representation, regularization or insufficient interaction data. The packet does not identify which explanation is responsible.

[Observed plus inference] Identical recorded m174 inputs differ by approximately 4.68/5.93 ml (704ba630f25fe7f20166, 92bac523bed1042d6a75). Missing covariates or experimental variability compete with deterministic response-surface explanations. Purposeful replication could clarify the m125 valley if an eligible matching record exists.

[ML prior] Matched contrasts identify local interactions; broader structural coverage tests transfer. Their value depends on Row frequency and measurement variability. Novelty, prediction scale and historical error alone do not determine expected accuracy gain.
coverage_or_redundancy_concerns: The supplied pool contains extensive familiar DCM/PE loading-solvent grids and exact duplicates. For example, m89 candidates 0141de34d99a6428ddd7 and f1bb0be6e913a5e26491 have identical recorded inputs. Compare molecule identity and all five condition fields; multiplicity represents Row frequency, not independent coverage.

Some legal candidates repeat observed inputs under another ID, including m92 10/1, sample 100 ul, EA 200 ul candidate ab1062a71079c605f750. Such measurements address variability rather than add a new recorded-input location.

m167, m147, m105, m160/m161 and several transition curves have substantial coverage. Unobserved m66, m36 and m119 offer interpretable transfer questions. Broader novel ketone, aldehyde, ether and halogenated grids remain exploration options, but novelty alone does not establish information value.

Overall Row accuracy also requires representative moderate-volume regions and systematic V1 errors. Adaptive historical errors overrepresent previously investigated neighborhoods; no unbiased Row error estimate or retrained performance measure is supplied.

warnings: Candidate IDs have predictions only. All measured evidence cited above comes from the supplied observed table. Premeasurement predictions and errors are historical, not current candidate errors.
Higher PE/EA is PE-richer and generally weaker on silica; 0/1 is pure EA. Loading-solvent identity is separate. Older stronger/weaker-eluent descriptions were reversed.
Sample volume and loading-solvent volume are distinct. Loading amount is derived from density and sample volume, preventing independent identification of sample-volume and mass effects here.
V2 minus V1 is elution interval width, not predictive uncertainty. Quantile widths, distance percentiles and similarity lack demonstrated calibration as expected-error measures.
